Listing fields vs icon art vs UIKit engineering

Alternate-icon apps blur three workstreams indie teams conflate:

  • App Store Connect listing metadata — name, subtitle, keywords, description, promotional text, screenshot overlay captions on the zh-Hans row. AppLocale scope.
  • Alternate icon assets & UIKit — PNG/JPEG icon files, CFBundleAlternateIcons, UIApplication.shared.setAlternateIconName, entitlement checks. Engineering and design scope — not AppLocale.
  • Screenshot composition — device frames, icon grids, re-exporting PNGs with burned-in icon set names or home-screen labels. Design scope — AppLocale delivers caption lines you paste or hand to a designer.

This page covers the first bucket for icon-customization-centric product pages. It is not our app name guide (the 30-character product title field only), not our generic screenshot captions guide (any gallery), and not our widget listing guide (Home Screen widgets are a different surface).

App name field vs alternate-icon display names

Two different strings buyers encounter:

  • App Store product name — the ~30-character title on the zh-Hans row that appears in Search and at the top of the product page. Covered by our App name in Simplified Chinese guide when that field alone needs work.
  • Alternate-icon display names — labels inside your in-app picker (“Classic”, “Midnight”, “Cherry Blossom”) and sometimes visible in marketing screenshots. These are not the Connect app name field. AppLocale can suggest zh-Hans display-name copy when you include your English icon set names in the listing brief — text only, not icon art.

Localizing the product name does not automatically fix picker labels or screenshot captions that still say Choose Icon in English.

Why icon-picker English hurts on the China storefront

Customization apps often lead marketing screenshots with the icon sheet, a themed icon grid, or a home-screen before/after — surfaces where system chrome and your icon set names appear together:

  • English frame headlines — “Choose Icon”, “App Icon”, “Customize” left as capture defaults while your zh-Hans description claims full Chinese support
  • Icon set names in screenshots — “Classic”, “Dark Mode”, “Neon”, “Winter” still in Latin script on gallery frames buyers skim before reading the description
  • Home-screen comparison labels — before/after frames with English micro-copy that does not match 图标 or 主题 search intent
  • Searchable fields still English — subtitle and keywords never packed for 图标, 主题, 深色模式, or category terms Chinese users actually type
  • In-app picker still English — public listing may be zh-Hans but runtime picker labels undermine the “localized app” impression

Better zh-Hans listing copy and icon-gallery captions reduce product-page bounce for customization-aware buyers — they do not replace UIKit localization inside the binary or guarantee Search rank.

Common mistakes on alternate-icon zh-Hans listings

  • Translating only the description — name, subtitle, and keywords still English while icon-picker screenshots dominate the gallery
  • Confusing app name with icon set names — stuffing picker labels like “Dark Icon” into the 30-character product title field instead of a proper subtitle
  • English icon names burned into PNG exports — Connect caption fields are zh-Hans but embedded set names on the image file are still Latin
  • Assuming icon assets localized = listing done — you shipped zh-Hans icon PNGs but the App Store row still falls back to English metadata
  • What's New still English after icon feature launch — see What's New in Simplified Chinese when alternate icons shipped in a recent version
  • Generic utility copy — description written for the core app with one sentence mentioning icons instead of naming customization workflows
  • ChatGPT 翻译腔 on customization jargon — literal translations of “alternate icon” or “icon pack” that native readers do not use in App Store copy

What good zh-Hans alternate-icon listing copy looks like

Listing fields should name the customization surfaces you actually ship — aligned with your screenshot order:

  • Subtitle — one concrete promise: “多款主题图标随心换” or “深色模式专属图标” — not vague “个性化体验”
  • Keywords — mix category terms with icon intent (图标, 主题, 深色) within Connect’s ~100-character zh-Hans budget; see Simplified Chinese keywords guide
  • Description — short paragraphs for seasonal sets, dark variants, and premium unlock icons — mirror screenshot sequence
  • Screenshot captions on icon-picker frames — name the on-screen action: “长按图标即可切换主题” not “强大功能”
  • Icon set name caption lines — when your gallery shows example set names, caption sheet lists zh-Hans equivalents for designer re-export or optional in-app copy reference
  • Voice consistency — same 你/您 choice as your description across overlay lines and promotional text

Connect checklist for alternate-icon apps targeting China

  1. Open App Store → Chinese (Simplified) — confirm the zh-Hans row exists; empty rows fall back to English on the China storefront
  2. Audit searchable fields — name, subtitle, keywords, description saved in zh-Hans, not placeholder English
  3. Walk the screenshot gallery in order — flag frames showing the icon picker sheet, themed icon grid, home-screen comparison, or set-name labels
  4. Export overlay lines — spreadsheet of English caption text per frame beats screenshots of Connect alone
  5. List English alternate-icon display names — if you want optional zh-Hans picker-name suggestions, include every set name from your in-app picker in the brief
  6. Note burned-in vs Connect captions — if icon set names are embedded in PNGs, caption deliverables go to your designer for re-export
  7. Match What's New if icons are new — release notes should mention icon customization in zh-Hans when that version added alternates
  8. Verify China in Pricing and Availability — storefront enabled before expecting zh-Hans to appear
